t: You're on Dean Bradley Street, in the City of Westminster. It's named after George Granville Bradley, who lived from 1821 to 1903. He was an English Anglican priest, scholar and schoolteacher. He was Master of University College, Oxford, from 1870 to 1881, and then Dean of Westminster from 1881 to 1902. The street carries his title as Dean, which fits, since Westminster Abbey's own community is the one he led.
